subject: Chemistry
title: Ricin: The Castor Bean Killer
description: One-minute skill: Ricin: The Castor Bean Killer.

hook.text: Castor oil is safe to drink. But the bean it comes from also contains ricin—one of the deadliest poisons known.

buildup.text: Ricin is a protein that enters cells and attacks ribosomes—the machinery that builds all other proteins.

discovery.text: One ricin molecule can destroy 1,500 ribosomes per minute. Without protein production, cells die.

twist.text: In 1978, a Bulgarian spy was assassinated with a ricin pellet fired from an umbrella on a London bridge.

climax.text: There is no antidote for ricin. Once it enters cells, the damage cannot be reversed.

punchline.text: One molecule shreds 1,500 ribosomes a minute. No antidote exists.

quiz.question: How does ricin kill cells?
options: It destroys ribosomes, stopping all protein production
It replaces DNA with non-functional copies

details.summary: Ricin is a potent toxin extracted from castor beans that kills cells by irreversibly inactivating ribosomes, halting all protein synthesis. A single ricin molecule can disable over 1,500 ribosomes per minute, and there is currently no approved antidote.
details.whyItMatters: Ricin's availability from a common plant and lack of antidote make it a persistent bioterrorism concern. It was famously used in the 1978 assassination of Bulgarian dissident Georgi Markov.
takeaways: Ricin destroys ribosomes, stopping all protein production in cells
Castor beans are widely grown, making ricin accessible globally
No approved antidote for ricin poisoning currently exists

faq.question: How was ricin used to assassinate Georgi Markov in 1978?
faq.answer: A modified umbrella tip injected a tiny platinum-iridium pellet containing ricin into Markov's leg on a London bridge. He developed a fever that evening and died three days later. The pellet was discovered during autopsy, revealing the assassination method.

faq.question: If castor beans contain ricin, why is castor oil considered safe?
faq.answer: Castor oil production involves pressing and heating the beans, which denatures the ricin protein. The extraction process separates oil from the protein-containing mash. Properly processed castor oil contains no active ricin and is safe for consumption and industrial use.
